pr_title: CMP: fix flag indicating the use of SSL/TLS for client-side HTTP connections
pr_body:
* CMP: fix `OSSL_CMP_MSG_http_perform()` by adding option `OSSL_CMP_OPT_USE_TLS`
* `OSSL_CMP_CTX_new.pod`: remove overlap with `OSSL_HTTP_transfer.pod`; improve the latter
* `apps/cmp.c`: `-tls_used` may be implied by `-server https:...`; improve related checks and doc

Fixes #21120 

##### Checklist
<!-- Remove items that do not apply. For completed items, change [ ] to [x]. -->
- [x] documentation is  added or updated
- [x] tests are added or updated
pr_comments: The two CI failures are unrelated.

> The two CI failures are unrelated.

Although unrelated the CMS failure looks really suspicious.

> > The two CI failures are unrelated.
> 
> Although unrelated the CMS failure looks really suspicious.

I agree the failing _CMS consistency tests_ on **buildbot/master:unix-ubuntu-aarch64** looked suspicious,
but luckily this disappeared after I rebased to the latest `master` half an hour ago.
I do not think this is a bug fix. Also what if anyone is already depending on the existing behavior of having the callback implying TLS?

> I do not think this is a bug fix.

As witnessed by #21120, the existing code has at least unexpected and undocumented behavior.
I see it as a bug because the use of the callback and its optional argument is needlessly limited to adding TLS (to the given CMP HTTP transfer).
If it is used in the CMP context for anything else, as can be done for the general (non-CMP) HTTP client, things go wrong as it is falsely assumed that TLS is being used (if the argument is non-NULL) or not being used (if the arg is NULL).

> Also what if anyone is already depending on the existing behavior of having the callback implying TLS?

This is indeed a problem, but I'd say the risk is small because it's an advanced feature and the existing behavior is weird and not documented.

> Also what if anyone is already depending on the existing behavior of having the callback implying TLS?

With this argument, we couldn't do any bug fixes because there might be someone who - for whatever strange reason - started relying on wrong behavior.

> > Also what if anyone is already depending on the existing behavior of having the callback implying TLS?
> 
> With this argument, we couldn't do any bug fixes because there might be someone who - for whatever strange reason - started relying on wrong behavior.

The app code already did this, what if someone just mimicked it? Can you please try harder to make this backwards compatible?

For example this could be a new feature for 3.2 where the OP is OSSL_CMP_OPT_NO_TLS and it switches off the tls if the callback is in use.

> > > Also what if anyone is already depending on the existing behavior of having the callback implying TLS?
> > 
> > With this argument, we couldn't do any bug fixes because there might be someone who - for whatever strange reason - started relying on wrong behavior.
> 
> The app code already did this, what if someone just mimicked it? Can you please try harder to make this backwards compatible?
> 
> For example this could be a new feature for 3.2 where the OP is OSSL_CMP_OPT_NO_TLS and it switches off the tls if the callback is in use.

Hmm, such a `OSSL_CMP_OPT_NO_TLS` option would only solve half of the problem.

Here is my proposal for a backward compatible solution:
define for the new `OSSL_CMP_OPT_USE_TLS` option a third value, namely -1, which is assumed by the default and means the hitherto behavior, where the callback function arg being non-NULL determines whether to use TLS.
When the `OSSL_CMP_OPT_USE_TLS` option is used and explicitly set to 0, TLS is not used, and when set to 1, TLS is used.

This way, the old behavior is by default, and explicitly setting the TLS leads to the expected new behavior.
Ok?
OK, but for master branch only.

> OK, but for master branch only.

Good, but why not also for at least 3.0?
As mentioned, the hitherto behavior is weird and not documented.
Doing the backport with the new solution does not harm existing code
and gives users of the 3.0 LTS version both a to-the-point doc and the chance to do the TLS (de-)selection in a proper way.
I would not block merging it to 3.1 and 3.0 if someone else approves it, but in my opinion this is clearly a new feature, not a bug fix.

Thanks @mattcaswell, @tmshort, and @t8m for your comments.
I've now implemented the newly proposed backward compatible solution for fixing #21120.

This also leaves room for potential future extensions of the mock server side towards TLS use.

> I'm ok with a back port to 3.1/3.0. Should this also be in master (not labeled for master, but the PR is on master)?

Pleased to hear.
I simply forgot to tick the `master` label - done now.

issue_context.title: Why is http_cb_arg used to determine whether to use tls in the CMP?
issue_context.body:
OpenSSL version：3.0
In OSSL_CMP_MSG_http_perform(),  use http_cb_arg to determine whether to use TLS. If http_cb is set but http_cb_arg is not set, the selection of the default port and https_proxy will be affected.
Must both http_cb and http_cb_arg be set?

**@crypto/cmp/cmp_http.c 71**
`tls_used = OSSL_CMP_CTX_get_http_cb_arg(ctx) != NULL;`
comments: Also please see the OSSL_CMP_CTX_set_http_cb_arg() manual page.

Generally, for the HTTP client functions like `OSSL_HTTP_transfer`,
the optional callback function `OSSL_HTTP_bio_cb_t bio_update_fn` and its optional argument `void *arg`
may be any function and argument value needed for manipulating the connection `BIO`.
The callback must be used in case TLS shall be added to the connection, i.e., to use HTTPS. 
See the man page of `OSSL_HTTP_bio_cb_t` for details.

The CMP client CLI implementation in `apps/cmp.c` uses the HTTP callback mechanism to set up the optional TLS layer of HTTP connection to the CMP server. Here the `http_cb_arg` points to information about the TLS layer such as an `SSL_CTX` pointer.

Good point that this is needlessly limiting and not sufficiently documented.
Indeed, if for the CMP client implementation the (default) HTTP transfer (implemented in `cmp_http.c`) is used,
the `http_cb_arg` must be non-NULL if and only if TLS is used.
So with the CMP client the HTTP callback mechanism so far cannot be used for anything else than for HTTPS.
It would have been better to have in the CMP context `OSSL_CMP_CTX` an independent flag
that tells whether TLS is used or not.
@lan1120 do you need to use the CMP HTTP callback mechanism for anything else than attaching TLS to HTTP?

@DDvO I think the modification of #21176 makes cmp tls_use clear.

Other:
We have a lot of scenarios where we need to set up our own bio for cmp:
If can set a customized bio for CMP_CTX and pass it to OSSL_HTTP_transfer in the OSSL_CMP_MSG_http_perform function, the usability is much better, because implementing a transfer_cb is expensive, although OSSL_HTTP_transfer is an external interface.

> @DDvO I think the modification of # 21176 makes cmp tls_use clear.

Pleased to hear. 

> Other: We have a lot of scenarios where we need to set up our own bio for cmp: If can set a customized bio for CMP_CTX and pass it to OSSL_HTTP_transfer in the OSSL_CMP_MSG_http_perform function, the usability is much better, because implementing a transfer_cb is expensive, although OSSL_HTTP_transfer is an external interface.
